complexity.notes: Membership test `key in self.stored`, `list.remove`, and `del self.stored[0]` are all O(n); the standard O(1) approach is a dict plus a doubly-linked list (or collections.OrderedDict). Also, eviction removes the key from `stored` but never from `self.cache`, so the dict leaks memory, growing with the total number of distinct keys ever inserted rather than staying bounded by capacity. The double `key in self.stored` in get is redundant.
complexity.summary: Uses a plain list `stored` to track recency order (front = least recent) plus a dict for values. Each get/put does a linear membership test and list.remove, so every operation is O(n) in the number of cached keys rather than the required O(1) average.
